hypothesis: Dynamic scheduling of one complete row at a time may reduce imbalance from rows with different Mandelbrot iteration counts compared with contiguous static row allocation. The serial branch avoids OpenMP overhead when the usable team is one; capping the team by height avoids requesting workers that cannot receive rows. The recurrence and per-pixel coordinate expressions remain unchanged.
notes: This is a dynamic-row scheduling candidate, not a measured speedup. It retains the input-bound coordinate calculations and recurrence, writes each pixel once, uses no global OpenMP setting changes, and requests no more than the supplied thread count. The controller should validate and measure it, including scheduling overhead.
transformations: Parallelize the outer row loop with OpenMP dynamic scheduling and chunk size one when the usable team has more than one thread.
Keep a serial nested-loop path for a one-thread usable team and cap the requested team size at the number of rows.
